title: Derived categories and derived functors
statement:
All derived categories are unbounded. For an abelian category $\mathcal C$, $D(\mathcal C)$
is the localization of the category of cochain complexes in $\mathcal C$ at the
quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its bounded below part
$D^+(\mathcal C)\subseteq D(\mathcal C)$ is the full subcategory of complexes whose
cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. Use the universes of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. K-injective means that every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic; K-flat means [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso], and Grothendieck abelian means [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. The total-derived-functor conventions are those of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Derived functors are total
derived functors on the unbounded categories, computed on resolutions:

- **Right derived functors.** Let $\mathcal C$ have K-injective resolutions, i.e. every
  complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex. Then every additive
  functor $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ to an abelian category has a total right
  derived functor $RF\colon D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$, computed by applying $F$
  termwise to a K-injective resolution. Every Grothendieck abelian category has
  K-injective resolutions.
- **Left derived functors.** Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal abelian category with the
  following properties: its tensor product is additive in each variable; it has
  countable coproducts and exact $\mathbf Z$-indexed colimits, and tensoring with a
  fixed object on either side preserves both these coproducts and these colimits; and it has functorial flat resolutions: a functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ with a natural epimorphism $P(M)\to M$ and flat values, where flat means that tensoring on either side preserves short exact sequences. Let
  $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and send quasi-isomorphisms between
  K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms. Then $F$ has a total left derived functor
  $LF\colon D(\mathcal C)\to D(\mathcal D)$, computed by applying $F$ termwise to a
  K-flat resolution. Pullback, tensor product and extension of scalars are derived
  this way.
- **Exact functors.** Under the respective existence hypotheses above, if $F$ is exact, then $RF\cong D(F)$ and $LF\cong D(F)$, where
  $D(F)$ applies $F$ termwise.
- **Derived adjunctions.** Let $f\colon\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D\colon g$ be
  an adjunction $f\dashv g$ of additive functors, with $f$ as in the second item and
  $\mathcal D$ with K-injective resolutions. Then $Lf\dashv Rg$.

Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The derived categories of this section are the following. In the final row, $\mathcal R$ is a commutative ring object of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$, for $\mathcal A$ as in the first row, and constructible means [def-sfb-constructible-module]. Bounded means that cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval; all the subcategories in the table are full.

| Category | Definition |
|---|---|
| $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ | $D(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A))$, finite coefficients (layer A). Here $\mathcal A$ is a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category and $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ carries the tensor product of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. |
| $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ | $D(\Mod(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),\Lambda_X))$, non-finite coefficients (layer B), for the ring object $\Lambda_X$ of [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and its module objects [det-def-sfb-module-objects]. For $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$ resp. $\underline E$ this is $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ resp. $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$. |
| $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ | the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology in $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$, with constructibility as just defined. No derived completeness condition is imposed. |

proof.text: Use the localization and its cohomology functors in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $D^+(\mathcal C)$ on objects $K$ for which some $a\in\mathbf Z$ satisfies $H^i(K)=0$ for all $i<a$. Quasi-isomorphic complexes have the same cohomology, so this is a condition on derived objects. The ambient category remains unbounded.

Apply the Right, Left and Exact clauses of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. They have precisely the respective hypotheses here: K-injective resolutions for the right functor; the stated monoidal colimits, their tensor preservation, functorial flat resolutions and preservation of K-flat quasi-isomorphisms for the left functor. Their resolution formulas are $RF(K)\cong F(I)$ and $LF(K)\cong F(P)$. Their exact-functor comparisons apply under these same existence hypotheses. The Grothendieck assertion in that statement supplies K-injective resolutions without boundedness.

For $f\dashv g$, apply the Derived adjunctions clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] with the identical source monoidal hypotheses on $f$ and the assumed K-injective resolutions in its target. It gives $Lf\dashv Rg$ on the unbounded categories. No assertion that $g$ preserves K-injectives or that $f$ preserves all quasi-isomorphisms is needed.

The first two table rows are those of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. In layer A, [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] and [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] both define tensor as sheafification of the objectwise tensor, with the sheafified unit. Hence the cited table uses the specified tensor here. In layer B, [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] sets $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ and transports its multiplication and unit. By [det-def-sfb-module-objects], objects are left actions of this ring object and arrows are action-compatible morphisms, with composition inherited from sheaves. These are exactly the objects, arrows and coefficient ring in the cited table. Thus its ambient derived category is $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ here as well. Taking $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O}_E$ or $\underline E$ gives the displayed abbreviations.

source.place: first two rows of the category table

proof.text: For the ring object in the last row, use the ambient module derived category in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use [def-sfb-constructible-module]: constructibility is a finite stratification on which the restricted module is locally finitely presented over the restricted ring object. Using the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], select the objects with this property for every $H^i$ and with $H^i=0$ outside a finite interval. Retain all ambient derived morphisms. This defines the final full subcategory, without using the later bounded-constructible node or imposing derived completeness.
